facts.t: India's most influential workplace law was written by judges
facts.d: The Vishaka guidelines governed sexual harassment at work for sixteen years, from 1997 until the POSH Act of 2013. A court filled a legislative vacuum, and Parliament eventually ratified what it had written.

facts.t: Article 142 lets the Supreme Court act without reasons
facts.d: The power to do complete justice permits relief and directions that need not be tethered to any statute or precedent. It is the single widest power any apex court in a common-law country holds — and the one most often cited in criticisms of overreach.

facts.t: There is nobody above the Supreme Court to correct it
facts.d: That asymmetry is the classical case for restraint: a district judge's error can be fixed on appeal, a High Court's in the Supreme Court, but the apex court's mistakes can only be undone by itself. Hence, as Justice Katju put it, the demand for utmost humility.

bank.q: With reference to methods of judicial activism, consider the following statements:
s: Public interest litigation rests on relaxed rules of locus standi.
Article 142 permits relief without detailed reasoning.
Suo motu cognisance is expressly conferred by Article 32.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Suo motu jurisdiction is exercised under Articles 32 and 226 but is not expressly conferred by them — it is judicially evolved.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (contribution):
pairs: 2. Guidelines on sexual harassment at work
bank.e: Vishaka on workplace harassment, D. K. Basu on arrest safeguards, Nilabati Behera on custodial violence, and Sunil Batra on solitary confinement.

bank.q: Which one of the following is listed as a positive impact of judicial activism?
o: Courts assuming administrative roles such as pollution monitoring
Bans on liquor sale along highways
Directing CBI autonomy in Vineet Narain
Redefining federal powers in NCT of Delhi v. UoI
bank.e: Vineet Narain is cited as executive accountability. The other three appear among the criticisms — institutional overlap, judicial populism and democratic erosion respectively.

bank.rs: Judges exercise wide corrective powers without an electoral mandate.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the counter-majoritarian objection in its judicial-activism form.

bank.q: Reference to international conventions in judicial reasoning draws on:
bank.e: Article 51(c), the Directive Principle on fostering respect for international law — the basis on which Vishaka drew on CEDAW.

bank.q: Consider the following components of judicial restraint:
s: Respecting precedent rather than readily overturning it.
Deferring to legislative intent, as in the same-sex marriage case.
Placing the burden of proof on the State to justify every statute.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Restraint works the other way — the presumption of constitutionality places the burden on the challenger.

bank.q: All of the following are criticisms of judicial activism EXCEPT:
o: Ad hoc rulings create legal uncertainty
Continuing mandamus enables sustained environmental oversight
bank.e: Continuing mandamus is cited as an innovative remedy among the positive impacts.

bank.q: Which case established that the burden of proof lies on the party seeking a change to the environmental status quo?
o: A. P. Pollution Control Board v. M. V. Nayudu
bank.e: A. P. Pollution Control Board v. M. V. Nayudu (1999) — an application of the precautionary principle to the burden of proof.

bank.q: With reference to judicial legislation by direction, consider the following:
s: Gaurav Jain concerned the education of children of prostitutes.
T. M. A. Pai addressed fee structures in professional colleges.
The Vishaka guidelines remained in force until Parliament legislated in 2013.
bank.e: All three are correct, and together they show the spectrum from filling a gap to setting detailed policy.

bank.q: Which jurisprudential theory did Justice Katju associate with judicial activism?
bank.e: Sociological jurisprudence, which he argued arms the judiciary with wide legislative and executive powers.

bank.as: The Supreme Court is urged to exercise its powers with utmost humility.
bank.rs: There is no forum above it to correct its errors.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the structural argument for restraint at the apex, distinct from the democratic one.
